title: Proxy-header trust tests cover only single-value X-Forwarded-For, so spoofed leftmost hops are untested
test: tests/serverIntegration.test.js: 'a spoofed leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry never grants loopback or trusted-LAN privilege to a remote rightmost hop' (real server, same environment as the main integration test, own server instance); tests/network.test.js: 'VAL-142: a multi-hop X-Forwarded-For chain from a peer that is not loopback is ignored'
proof: Production already reads X-Forwarded-For from the right since TASK-005 (e640d25), so the new integration test passes on the current code and no production change was needed (the prompt's 'todo' branch does not apply). It fails on the code before TASK-005 (09c6162, a throwaway worktree with the new test file copied in): GET /api/metrics with 'x-forwarded-for: 127.0.0.1, 203.0.113.140' returns 200 instead of 403 ('200 !== 403'). With the metrics block removed from the copy it fails next on create-room: a socket sending '127.0.0.1, 203.0.113.151' is allowed to create a room without an operator token ('true !== false'); with that block removed too it fails on join-room: '192.168.50.125, 203.0.113.161' gets relayAllowed true ('true !== false'). So each of the three parts (metrics, create-room, relay policy) fails on the old code. The test also pins the other direction: a remote leftmost entry with a loopback or trusted-LAN rightmost hop ('203.0.113.141, 127.0.0.1' on /api/metrics gives 200; '203.0.113.164, 192.168.50.126' gives relayAllowed true), so it shows the rightmost hop is what counts, not 'any remote entry'. The unit test needs no failing run: it pins current behaviour of the exported helper getTrustedForwardedClientIp for non-loopback peers (the header is ignored whatever the chain says); the integration server only accepts connections from its own loopback peer, so a non-loopback peer can only be tested at that level.
